title: Validation Service — Performance & Load
description: Prestaties en belasting van de Validation Service, rechtstreeks uit de applicatiedatabase (datasource: DEV Postgres, uid devpg). Doorlooptijd = klok van aanmelden tot klaar (inclusief wachten in de wachtrij). Verwerkingstijd = som van de taakduren (alleen echt rekenwerk).

panels.title: Duration per task type over time (daily average)
panels.description: How long does each validation step take on average per day? Based on ifc_validation_task.ended - started. Follows the dashboard time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(t.started, '1d'),
  t.type AS metric,
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.ended - t.started)))::numeric, 1) AS duration_s
FROM ifc_validation_task t
WHERE $__timeFilter(t.started)
  AND t.started IS NOT NULL
  AND t.ended IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Validation requests per day (by final status)
panels.description: Volume: how many files are submitted per day, and how they ended (COMPLETED / FAILED / PENDING / INITIATED). Source: ifc_validation_request.created.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(r.created, '1d'),
  r.status AS metric,
  COUNT(*)::float AS requests
FROM ifc_validation_request r
WHERE $__timeFilter(r.created)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Failure rate per task type
panels.description: Which validation step breaks most often? Failure rate = FAILED / (FAILED + COMPLETED) within the selected time range. Tasks with status SKIPPED / N/A / INITIATED are excluded.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  t.type                                                                   AS task_type,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.status IN ('COMPLETED','FAILED'))               AS completed,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.status = 'FAILED')                             AS failed,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.status = 'FAILED')
        / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.status IN ('COMPLETED','FAILED')), 0), 2) AS failure_rate_pct,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t.status IN ('PENDING','INITIATED'))             AS unfinished
FROM ifc_validation_task t
WHERE $__timeFilter(t.created)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 4 DESC NULLS LAST, 2 DESC

panels.title: Processing time vs file size
panels.description: Does it get slower as files get larger? Files are grouped into size buckets; per bucket the average and p95 of processing time (sum of task durations).

targets.rawSql:
WITH per_request AS (
  SELECT r.id,
         r.size,
         SUM(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.ended - t.started))) AS processing_time_s
  FROM ifc_validation_request r
  JOIN ifc_validation_task t ON t.request_id = r.id
  WHERE $__timeFilter(r.created)
    AND r.size IS NOT NULL
    AND t.started IS NOT NULL
    AND t.ended IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY r.id, r.size
)
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN size <   1048576 THEN '1. < 1 MB'
    WHEN size <   5242880 THEN '2. 1-5 MB'
    WHEN size <  20971520 THEN '3. 5-20 MB'
    WHEN size <  52428800 THEN '4. 20-50 MB'
    WHEN size < 209715200 THEN '5. 50-200 MB'
    ELSE                       '6. > 200 MB'
  END                                                                          AS size,
  ROUND(AVG(verwerkingstijd_s)::numeric, 0)                                    AS avg_s,
  ROUND(percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY verwerkingstijd_s)::numeric, 0) AS p95_s,
  COUNT(*)                                                                     AS count
FROM per_request
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Lead time per request (p50 / p95 per day)
panels.description: How long does a user actually wait? Lead time = completed - created of the request, so including queue time. Large outliers mean queueing or re-runs, not slow validation.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  $__timeGroupAlias(r.created, '1d'),
  ROUND(percentile_cont(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.completed - r.created)))::numeric, 1) AS p50_s,
  ROUND(percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.completed - r.created)))::numeric, 1) AS p95_s
FROM ifc_validation_request r
WHERE $__timeFilter(r.created)
  AND r.completed IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: 20 slowest requests (last 30 days)
panels.description: Fixed 30-day window, independent of the time range above. Sorted by processing time (sum of task durations). Lead time is shown alongside: a large gap between the two means waiting, not working.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  r.created                                                        AS submitted,
  r.file_name                                                      AS file,
  ROUND(r.size / 1048576.0, 1)                                     AS mb,
  r.status,
  ROUND(v.processing_time_s::numeric, 0)                                AS processing_time_s,
  ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.completed - r.created))::numeric, 0)  AS lead_time_s,
  v.langzaamste_taak
FROM ifc_validation_request r
JOIN (
  SELECT t.request_id,
         SUM(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.ended - t.started)))                    AS processing_time_s,
         (ARRAY_AGG(t.type ORDER BY (t.ended - t.started) DESC))[1]        AS slowest_task
  FROM ifc_validation_task t
  WHERE t.started IS NOT NULL AND t.ended IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY t.request_id
) v ON v.request_id = r.id
WHERE r.created > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
ORDER BY v.processing_time_s DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 20

panels.title: Most expensive gherkin rules (total CPU time, cumulative)
panels.description: From the gherkin logs on the NFS share (201k measurements since Dec 2025), ingested nightly by perf-metrics/gherkin_rule_timings.sh. NOTE: this is CPU time (time.process_time), not wall-clock time, so I/O wait is not included. Logged in PRODUCTION mode only.

panels.title: Rule cost: total, average and longest run
panels.description: Average versus longest run shows the skew: a few large models dominate. A rule with a low average but an extreme maximum is a tail risk.

panels.title: Outcomes per rule (top 15, whole DB)
panels.description: Which rules produce the most outcomes (severity WARNING/ERROR)? Feeds backlog item F4: SWE001 and IFC105 together account for ~1.7M of the ~5M rows.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN regel ~ '^[A-Z]{2,5}[0-9]{2,3}$' THEN regel
       ELSE '(SCHEMA check, not a gherkin rule)' END AS rule,
  SUM(warnings)::bigint AS warnings,
  SUM(errors)::bigint  AS errors,
  SUM(totaal)::bigint  AS total
FROM (
  SELECT split_part(feature, ' ', 1) AS rule,
         SUM((severity = 3)::int) AS warnings,
         SUM((severity = 4)::int) AS errors,
         COUNT(*) AS total
  FROM ifc_validation_outcome
  WHERE severity >= 3 AND feature IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1
) sub
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY totaal DESC
LIMIT 15
